text:
jess: FYI customer BeaconApps is seeing 429s + 2–3s token latency on Dedicated tier. They reported spike at ~11:02 UTC. Ticket #CS-9872. Appears autoscaler didn't add capacity fast enough.
kevin: Can you paste the probe logs and the tenant's Dedicated config? minReplicas, burst policy, any reserved headroom?
jess: Config from tenant page: `minReplicas: 2`, `maxReplicas: 50`, `burstPolicy: reserved-burst`, `reservedCapacity: 0`. Also they have quota for 8 GPUs total in the region.
jess: Logs from probe controller (snip):
```
2025-06-04T11:01:58Z probe: healthcheck=ok
2025-06-04T11:02:01Z probe: spike detected, probe_fanout=80
2025-06-04T11:02:04Z autoscaler: scale_decision=add, desired=12, reason=throughput
2025-06-04T11:02:04Z orchestrator: allocate_request->pending (imagePullBackoff? no) -> awaiting VM
2025-06-04T11:02:12Z autoscaler: provision_timeout
2025-06-04T11:02:20Z user-api: 429 upstream (scale not ready)
```
kevin: Looks like provisioning timed out ~8s between allocate and ready; orchestration shows pending VM handshake lingered. Any evidence of image pull or registry auth issues?
jess: No image errors — images already hot in the region. Curious thing: `probe_fanout=80` but our headroom estimator only recommended +10 replicas. Maybe noisy neighbor made running pods slower so each replica handled less qps. Customer load was a short burst (1500 RPS for ~10s) — saw token latencies spike.
tara: Could be metric aggregation lag causing the autoscaler to under-estimate needed capacity. We're currently using a 15s sliding window for qps; a 10s microburst can be masked. Also seen similar once where headroom metric p95 was out-of-date due to delayed metric push from model pods.
oliver: Oncall: can you confirm if metric-agent had any backlog? Also check if the autoscaler held a `scale_cooldown` incorrectly for this tenant.
sre-oncall: metrics pipeline shows ingestion lag ~12s at 11:02 (region eu-west-1). There's a backlog spike aligning with the burst. Agent pods were CPU-throttled (OOMThrottle) for a few minutes prior — noisy tenant labelled `tenant=staccato-inc` had heavy GPU ops causing node starvation.
jess: That matches customer report: they share the Dedicated cluster with a few high-throughput tenants. BeaconApps was running large batch transforms earlier today.
kevin: Two potential root causes: 1) metric ingestion lag -> undercount qps -> low desired replica estimate; 2) noisy neighbor causing node provisioning delays / VM queueing -> provisioning timeout. Both contributed.
jess: Repro steps I ran in staging to reproduce failure:
  1) Deploy dedicated-sim tenant with `minReplicas:2` and autoscaler sliding window 15s.
  2) From loadgen host run: `wrk -t12 -c600 -d15s http://dedicated-host/generate` (burst 1500 rps approximate)
  3) Watch `/metrics` for `probe_fanout` and autoscaler `desired_replicas` logs.
Result: autoscaler recommended +8 but metric lag and backend queueing pushed actual provision -> timeout -> 429s for ~10–20s.
oliver: Good repro. Mitigation options:
  - Short term (support): manually increase `minReplicas` to 6 for BeaconApps and enable `reservedCapacity: 4` to prevent headroom misestimates. Also open a temporary quota increase so orchestration can provision faster.
  - Mid term (eng): reduce autoscaler sliding window to 5s for short-burst-sensitive tenants OR supplement with burst detector that alarm-boosts desired_replicas immediately.
  - Infra: investigate noisy tenant scheduling and enforce QoS (cgroup CPU shares) and preemptible throttling so agent/metric pods don't get CPU-starved.
kevin: Also add an alert for `metrics_ingest_lag > 7s` per-region and `autoscaler_provision_timeout` to paging.
jess: For CS immediate: I raised minReplicas and reservedCapacity, customer saw error rate drop to 0 within ~40s after override. They asked for a workaround to avoid future hits.
oliver: I'll own the engineering ticket to implement burst detector + faster fallback policy. Filed ENG-3245 and linked CS-9872. Will also add unit/integration test that simulates metric lag.
tara: Can someone collect node kubelet logs and the orchestration VM queue trace for 11:00–11:05? ops-bot: run `collect-dedicated-dump --tenant beaconapps --since 2025-06-04T11:00:00Z --until 2025-06-04T11:06:00Z` and attach to ENG-3245.
ops-bot: dump started -> s3://redwood-debug/ENG-3245/beaconapps-20250604.tgz (will complete ~2m)
jess: Also proposed short doc for CS: "Dedicated warm-pool recommendations" — I can draft and share with customers who have bursty traffic.
kevin: Quick note: set a conservative default `reservedCapacity: 1` for all Dedicated tenants to reduce first-hit 429s until burst detector is in.
oliver: Assigning myself to ENG-3245. Will push an RFC for burst detector this week.
jess: Thanks all — marking this thread triaged. Follow-up: postmortem if recurrence within 30 days. :white_check_mark:
